newsitem.title: CHINA: Korea First debt seen worst hit by S&P.
newsitem.headline: Korea First debt seen worst hit by S&P.

text.p: The announcement by Standard and Poor's Corp that it might cut the ratings of five South Korean banks is expected to hit Korea First Bank the hardest, analysts said on Wednesday.
"Korea First Bank is definitely affected most" said Albert Jan Hofman, head of Asian fixed income research at ABN Amro Hoare Govett.
Hofman said the bank is heavily exposed to a number of financially troubled Korean conglomerates, including the Jinro, Hanbo, Samni and Kia groups.

S&P said in a statement that its rating action reflected the deteriorating asset quality and heightening industry risks faced by Korean banks as defaults continue to emerge among Korea's industrial conglomerates.
The overall deterioration of asset quality has recently been demonstrated by the collapse of the Kia group, it said.
Korea First Bank is the largest creditor of the Kia Group.
Its exposure to the Hanbo Group roughly equals the value of the bank's consolidated equity, S&P said in April.
Korea First Bank's long-term debt is currently rated BBB-minus by S&P. The rating agency cut the bank's ratings to that level from BBB-plus in April in a rare two-notch move.
If S&P were to downgrade Korea First Bank by another notch, the bank would immediately become speculative grade.
Traders said Korea First Bank's outstanding one-year paper could widen by 10 basis points in reaction to the S&P move.
They said the one-year notes are currently offered at a huge spread of 170 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate, but there are no bids.
KFB's one-year paper has widened by 20 basis points since Kia Group announced its loan problems earlier this year. There is almost no liquidity in KFB's longer-dated paper.

In comparison, Hanil Bank -- which also was put on negative watch by S&P -- last week launched a floating rate note issue that gave an all-in return of 54.5 basis points for an effective tenor of two years.
In addition to Korea First Bank, S&P said it may cut Hanil Bank, Korea Long-Term Credit Bank, Shinhan Bank and Korea Exchange Bank.
Hanil and Korea Long are currently rated A-minus for their long-term debt and A-2 for their short-term debt. Shinhan is rated Single-A/A-1, while KEB has a short-term rating of A-2.
S&P said the five banks are among private-sector creditors to the Kia group with aggregate exposure of about 1.7 trillion Korean won.
